validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed real. Two independent US-government primary sources document this exact project: (1) EIA's own 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' pipeline-projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, downloaded and parsed directly with openpyxl rather than relying on the wiki's cited generic eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php navigation page, which is not itself citable) carries a row named exactly 'Putnam Expansion Project', Pipeline Operator Name 'Florida Gas Transmission', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2022-02-25, Docket CP19-474, Cost(millions) 102.6, Miles 20.7, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 169, Diameter 30. (2) FERC's own Federal Register notices for Docket CP19-474-000 - Notice of Application (govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-06-18/pdf/2019-12813.pdf, filed May 31, 2019), Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-08-20/pdf/2019-17896.pdf), and Notice of Availability of the Environmental Assessment (govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-12-12/pdf/2019-26759.pdf) - independently describe Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC's application to construct a 13.7-mile West Loop and a 7.0-mile East Loop of 30-inch pipe in Columbia, Union, Clay, Putnam, and Orange counties, Florida, to serve growing power-generation demand (Seminole Electric Cooperative). Note: federalregister.gov's own page and PDF path were blocked/404 to scripted fetches - all three notices were retrieved instead via their govinfo.gov/content/pkg/... PDF mirrors, confirmed real PDFs and extracted with pdftotext -layout. A third independent line of confirmation - EIA's own editorial coverage (Today in Energy, eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=52478, and the Natural Gas Weekly Update archive for 2022-05-19) - describes the Putnam Expansion (169 MMcf/d = 0.17 Bcf/d) entering service in Q1 2022, consistent with the workbook's 2022-02-25 completion date. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a genuine FGT interstate natural-gas TRANSMISSION-loop expansion (real new pipe, not a phantom/GEM-only entity, not gathering/processing) - the FERC filings describe NGA-regulated interstate transportation capacity additions via looping, and this is properly a physical-pipe expansion (LengthKnown/Diameter both populated, per the standing convention), unlike some other FGT-family expansion rows in this batch that are compression-only (LengthKnown=0). DUPLICATE: checked against all other Florida Gas Transmission-family roster rows in this batch (P2529 East Louisiana Project, P2627 Mobile Bay Lateral Expansion, P2738 South Alabama Project, P4028-P4040 and P4050/P4060, the Phase IV-VIII/AE-Cooperative/Turkey-Point/East-Leg/Alabama-Power-Lateral/Sanford/Southwest-Alabama rows) via the fresh GGIT snapshot (2026-09-04) and the worklist's pipeline_name/segment_name pairing - none of these carry the Putnam Expansion Project name, docket (CP19-474), or overlapping county geography; no duplicate/relabel concern. Cross-referenced EIA's full FGT-family project list (22 rows) against the roster and found it maps cleanly 1:1 to all 18 other FGT rows in this batch by project name, with three EIA-listed FGT projects (East-West Project/CP17-8, Galveston County Project/CP20-505, Mobile County Project/CP22-12) and one cancelled project (Big Bend Project/CP21-45) that do NOT correspond to any roster PID in this batch - flagged as cross_row_leads below for a possible Discovery/scope check, not claimed as evidence against THIS row. ATTRIBUTION: Owner (Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC, 100%) and Location (Florida-to-Florida, no state-border crossing) both confirmed correct; Operator was blank and is filled with 'Energy Transfer' below - see the Owner/Operator/Location fills for full sourcing. Opened all 9 of this row's harvested wiki citations (shared across the whole FGT-family wiki page): #1 (A Barrel Full) is banned, never used; #5 (the wiki's cited kindermorgan.com FGT page) is CONFIRMED DEAD (404 via curl) - I did not force a Wayback capture of the dead page since a live, better replacement (kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index) was found and used instead; #3/#4/#6/#8/#12 are all instances of the same generic eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php navigation page (not citable on its own, but it correctly points toward EIA's data - I went to the actual underlying workbook/articles instead); #9 (oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491) is for the main FGT trunk, not Putnam specifically, and Putnam's own oilandgaswatch page (/pipeline/3352) is an empty JS shell (403/no server-rendered content) - not usable either way; #7 (fractracker.org) and #10 (a Pipeline & Gas Journal PDF on s3) and #11 (texasenergyreport.com, an unrelated East-West Pipeline Expansion article) were opened and found not to add project-specific facts beyond what FERC/EIA already provided. All facts used in this shard come from FERC's own docket filings and EIA's independently-maintained data, not from any wiki-harvested citation.

validity.recommendation: correct LengthKnown from 30.30 km to 33.31 km (equivalently, 20.7 mi to match the sibling FGT rows' 'mi' unit convention) - the sheet's current figure is not supported by either primary source and both agree closely with each other on a materially longer length.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current LengthKnown=30.30 km does not match either of the two independent primary sources found for this specific project: FERC's own Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-08-20/pdf/2019-17896.pdf, Docket CP19-474) describes a 13.7-mile West Loop plus a 7.0-mile East Loop = 20.7 miles total; EIA's independently-maintained 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' workbook lists Miles=20.7 for the same project/docket. 20.7 mi = 33.31 km, a ~9.9% increase over the sheet's 30.30 km. I could not find any source, including the wiki's own citation pool, supporting 30.30 km (which back-converts to ~18.83 mi, matching neither loop individually nor their sum) - this appears to be a genuine data error, not a scope/definition difference (unlike, e.g., a system-vs-segment ambiguity). Recommend Update correct the value to 33.31 km, or convert to miles (20.70 mi) to match the 'mi' unit convention used by every other Florida Gas Transmission-family row in this batch (P2627, P2738, P4028-P4040, P4050, P4060 all record LengthKnownUnits='mi'; P2594 alone uses 'km') - flagging both the value error and the unit-convention inconsistency for Baird's judgment on which correction path to take.
